items.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd Stock (TSM) Moved Down by 3.11% on Aug 24: Facts Behind the Movement
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSM) stock declined by 3.11% on August 24, primarily due to investor profit-taking after a significant rally in the semiconductor sector, exacerbated by concerns over heavy capital expenditures and valuation. Technical indicators show a MACD sell signal and an oversold Williams %R, while fundamental analysis highlights substantial revenue and net profit figures within the Technology Equipment industry. Key risks include surging capital expenditure, valuation premia, geopolitical concentration, and operational complexities from international expansion.

items.title: DA Davidson raises Emerson stock price target on power demand outlook
items.summary: DA Davidson has increased its price target for Emerson Electric Co. (NYSE:EMR) to $155 from $145, maintaining a Neutral rating, due to slightly higher fiscal year 2027 estimates and confidence in Emerson's strong position in the current upcycle. The new target is based on 18.9 times the firm's fiscal year 2028 EPS forecast of $8.20, with the stock currently trading above this target. Emerson is well-positioned to meet its 2025 targets, supported by secular tailwinds such as increasing power generation demands and LNG investment, despite risks from project delays and geopolitical headwinds.

items.title: Applied Materials Inc Stock (AMAT) Opened Down by 3.02% on Aug 24: What Investors Need To Know
items.summary: Applied Materials Inc (AMAT) stock opened down by 3.02% despite reporting record quarterly earnings driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. The decline is attributed to high investor expectations, profit-taking, and concerns over near-term margin headwinds from expansion costs and capital expenditures. Technical indicators show a MACD sell signal, and analysts have set an average price target of $635.01, with identified risks including margin stagnation, lack of long-term revenue visibility, and geopolitical trade exposure.

items.title: Morgan Stanley warns bond yields could rise in post-WWII-style era
items.summary: Morgan Stanley is cautioning investors that bond yields may continue to rise, citing a shift in economic cycles that resembles the post-World War II era. The investment bank believes market dynamics have moved away from the disinflationary period observed from 1982 to 2020. This prediction was initially made by Morgan Stanley in 2021, suggesting a sustained change in economic conditions.

items.title: Managing Risk in the Infrastructure Project Lifecycle
items.summary: The article discusses the increasing volatility and complexity of the geopolitical environment, which significantly impacts infrastructure projects. It outlines a lifecycle framework for managing these risks, emphasizing continuous assessment, integrated risk management, and proactive engagement across dealmaking, permitting, construction, and operations. The piece concludes by highlighting the critical role of the legal team in leading these integrated efforts to turn volatility into a competitive advantage.

items.title: Precious Metals StoneX Bullion weekly round-up; bond yields, debasement; conflicting influences on gold
items.summary: This StoneX Bullion weekly round-up analyzes the conflicting influences on gold prices, noting that an exogenous shock from a Treasury announcement spurred a rally, yet rising bond yields act as a headwind. The report details the impact of the Treasury's intervention in long-term bond markets, increasing U.S. debt, and the dollar's defensive stance, all of which generally support gold. Despite this, gold's momentum is tempered by bond activity, with the long-term outlook dependent on geopolitics and financial management.

items.title: Cost to Ship a VLCC Through Hormuz Hits $20 Million, TotalEnergies CEO Says
items.summary: TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne stated that shipping oil on a supertanker through the Strait of Hormuz costs around $20 million, translating to about $10 a barrel. This high freight cost creates significant profit margins for traders and shipowners, as producers sell oil inside the Persian Gulf at $50-$60 per barrel due to ongoing conflict. Despite fears of price surges, increased oil flows through Hormuz have kept benchmark Brent futures below $100, while fuel markets remain tight due to attacks on Russian refineries.

items.title: Caterpillar's Q2 Adjusted Operating Margin Rebounds: Is the Worst Over?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) saw a significant rebound in its Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin, expanding 430 basis points year-over-year to 21.9%, driven by higher sales volumes and favorable pricing despite increased costs and tariffs. The company has raised its 2026 sales and revenue outlook to mid-to-high teens growth and expects full-year adjusted operating margin to improve meaningfully from 2025. While peers like Terex and Komatsu faced margin declines due to similar cost and tariff pressures, Caterpillar's stock has outperformed the industry, and its earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 show strong growth.

items.title: Frontline Approaches 14-Year Peak as Oil Climbs 6% on the Week
items.summary: Frontline shares are nearing a 14-year high, trading just 3.3% below their 52-week peak, driven by a 6% weekly surge in oil prices and tightening tanker availability due to Strait of Hormuz shipping constraints. Unlike major integrated oil producers like Exxon and Chevron, Frontline provides more direct exposure to these market dynamics, resulting in a 5.97% stock increase last week. The company, set to announce Q2 results on August 31, is operating on solid financial ground, having reported strong Q1 adjusted earnings and a dividend in line with EPS.

items.title: Bernstein SocGen maintains StandardAero stock rating after Q2 results
items.summary: Bernstein SocGen has reaffirmed its Outperform rating and $39.00 price target for StandardAero Inc (NYSE:SARO) following the company's second-quarter earnings report, noting solid revenues but short-term margin issues. Despite a recent stock decline and margin pressure, Bernstein SocGen suggests the stock appears undervalued and that StandardAero should be insulated from short-term oil price movements. The company reported a 4.6% revenue increase, 24% adjusted earnings rise, and an uplifted full-year 2026 outlook.
